rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ecology studies the interactions between organisms and their environment. Biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) factors shape every ecosystem. Species interact through mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation, and competition.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Ecosystem = Biotic (producers + consumers + decomposers) + Abiotic (light, water, soil, gases)
Species interactions: mutualism (+/+), commensalism (+/0), parasitism (+/-), predation (+/-), competition (-/-)
Energy flow: Sun → Producer → Primary consumer → Secondary consumer → ... → Heat (unidirectional)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Predation (+/-) and parasitism (+/-) both harm one partner; predation usually KILLS the prey quickly, parasitism is long-term and usually does not kill the host immediately.  ·  Mutualism (+/+) benefits both; commensalism (+/0) benefits one, affects neither; parasitism (+/-) benefits one, harms the other.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a clear biotic/abiotic distinction and the 5 species interactions with examples.  ·  Structural vs functional aspects of an ecosystem are a very common long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Pond ecosystem: phytoplankton (producer) → zooplankton (herbivore) → small fish (carnivore) → big fish; bacteria + fungi (decomposer).  ·  Forest ecosystem: trees + grass (producers) → deer, insects (herbivores) → tiger, owl (carnivores) → fungi, bacteria (decomposers).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Competition (-/-) harms BOTH species (interspecific); intra-specific competition is within the same species.  ·  An ecosystem is a FUNCTIONAL unit (energy flow + nutrient cycling); a community is just the assemblage of species.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Ecology: study of organism-environment interactions.  ·  Biotic (living) vs abiotic (non-living) factors.  ·  Species interactions: mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation, competition.  ·  Ecosystem = biotic + abiotic; types: aquatic + terrestrial.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A single hectare of a tropical forest can contain 100+ tree species.  ·  The sun is the primary energy source of almost all ecosystems.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the functional aspects of a forest ecosystem.  ·  Explain energy flow in an ecosystem.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Give a Nepali example for each ecosystem type.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Mutualism: bee + flower; commensalism: barnacle + whale; parasitism: tapeworm + human.  ·  Competition: two grass species competing for light in a meadow.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A barnacle living on a whale (harmed neither, barnacle benefits) is an example of: → B  ·  Energy in an ecosystem flows: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Ecology: the study of the interactions between organisms and their environment (biotic + abiotic).  ·  Biotic factors: living components (plants, animals, microorganisms); Abiotic factors: non-living (light, temperature, water, soil, pH, gases).  ·  Species interactions: mutualism (+/+), commensalism (+/0), parasitism (+/-), predation (+/-), competition (-/-), amensalism (-/0), neutralism (0/0).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Pond/forest ecosystems  ·  Structural: producers, consumers, decomposers; trophic levels.  ·  Functional: energy flow (unidirectional) + nutrient cycling (biogeochemical).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Pond and forest ecosystems: Nepal examples.  ·  Energy flows ONEDIRECTIONALLY through an ecosystem (sun → producers → consumers → heat); it is NOT cycled.  ·  Nutrients (C, N, P) ARE cycled (biogeochemical); energy is not cycled.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Energy flows unidirectionally; nutrients cycle — a key exam contrast.  ·  Give a Nepali example (pond, forest, Chitwan) for each ecosystem.  ·  Memorise the 5 species interactions with one example each.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Learn the structural aspects (producers, consumers, decomposers).  ·  Explain the functional aspects (energy flow + nutrient cycling).  ·  Describe a pond and a forest ecosystem with Nepali examples.
